upstream_source_register.cite: Daane, J. M. et al. (2021). Curr. Biol. PMC9172250: lat4a x kcnh2a interaction phenocopying flying-fish fin proportion in zebrafish; genome-wide signatures across 35 species.
upstream_source_register.note: A bioelectric and amino-acid-transport signalling interaction (lat4a, kcnh2a) that phenocopies flying-fish fin proportion in ZEBRAFISH, plus genome-wide signatures across 35 species. The functional demonstration is in zebrafish; the flying-fish side is association.
caveats: Cross-organism transfer: this does not establish that enlarging a halfbeak's fins is experimentally grounded. It is an unestablished transfer hypothesis.
A testable mechanism for a bigger paired fin; no flight is implied.
Title and author list are not restated here because the card did not carry them; only the journal, year and PMC id were given.

upstream_source_register.cite: Darwin, C. (1859). On the Origin of Species, Chapter VI. Project Gutenberg #1228 (also 22764, 2009).

upstream_source_register.cite: Davenport, J. (1992). Wing-loading, stability and morphometric relationships in flying fish (Exocoetidae) from the North-eastern Atlantic. J. Mar. Biol. Assoc. UK 72(1): 25-39.
upstream_source_register.read_level: abstract, as returned by a fetch tool
upstream_source_register.note: Pectoral fin length cannot exceed 78-79% of standard length without impairing swimming. Pelvic fins of four-winged forms solve pitch stability. Oxyporhamphus micropterus has high wing loading but cannot take off because the centre of gravity lies behind the pectorals.
caveats: Full text paywalled; the DOI is as recorded by the report and was not opened for this page.
No URL is given: the DOI was not recorded in the report, and this page does not guess one.

upstream_source_register.cite: Fish, F. E. (1990). Wing design and scaling of flying fish with regard to flight performance. J. Zool. 221: 391-403.
upstream_source_register.note: n = 199 preserved specimens, 33 species, 6 genera. The report read the extracted PDF text directly.
caveats: Text gives overall maximum pectoral aspect ratio 16.9; Table III gives Exocoetus 8.9-19.9. They disagree; both are shown.
Results text gives a 0.001 kg Hirundichthys as the lowest wing loading while the stated specimen range starts at 0.003 kg. Unresolved.
Re-read from the PDF (p.395) by the research lead: 3.0-16.9 is the INDIVIDUAL pectoral-fin aspect ratio; Table III reaches 19.9 for Exocoetus. Park & Choi measured 9.0-10.7 for the same quantity.
